experiments.title: Filter so the engine can skip data
experiments.question: Count and sum the events of one day out of 100.

variants.name: text formatting around the column
variants.sql: SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(amount) FROM events WHERE strftime(ts, '%Y-%m-%d') = '2026-02-19'

variants.name: date_trunc around the column
variants.sql: SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(amount) FROM events WHERE date_trunc('day', ts) = TIMESTAMP '2026-02-19'

variants.name: half-open range on the raw column
variants.sql: SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(amount) FROM events WHERE ts >= TIMESTAMP '2026-02-19' AND ts < TIMESTAMP '2026-02-20'

variants.name: filter on the partition column
variants.sql: SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(amount) FROM events WHERE event_date = DATE '2026-02-19'

experiments.title: Keep the latest version of each key
experiments.question: Count the orders and sum their latest amounts (about 1.25 versions per order).

variants.name: ROW_NUMBER ... rn = 1 over all history
variants.sql: SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(amount) FROM (SELECT amount, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY ts DESC) AS rn FROM events) WHERE rn = 1

variants.name: arg_max ... GROUP BY over all history
variants.sql: SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(amount) FROM (SELECT arg_max(amount, ts) AS amount FROM events GROUP BY order_id)

variants.name: ROW_NUMBER over the newest day only
variants.sql: SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(amount) FROM (SELECT amount, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY ts DESC) AS rn FROM events WHERE event_date = DATE '2026-04-10') WHERE rn = 1

experiments.title: Aggregate before a dimension join, or after
experiments.question: Revenue per user segment: events joined to a 2,000,000-row user table.

variants.name: join, then aggregate
variants.sql: SELECT u.segment, SUM(e.amount) FROM events AS e JOIN users AS u USING (user_id) GROUP BY u.segment ORDER BY 1

variants.name: aggregate per user, then join
variants.sql: WITH per_user AS (SELECT user_id, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM events GROUP BY user_id) SELECT u.segment, SUM(p.amount) FROM per_user AS p JOIN users AS u USING (user_id) GROUP BY u.segment ORDER BY 1

experiments.title: Answer a dashboard from a summary table
experiments.question: Revenue per day and city for the last 30 days.

variants.name: from the raw events
variants.sql: SELECT event_date, city_id, SUM(amount) FROM events WHERE event_date >= DATE '2026-03-12' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY ALL

variants.name: from a daily summary table
variants.sql: SELECT event_date, city_id, SUM(revenue) FROM daily_city WHERE event_date >= DATE '2026-03-12' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY ALL

experiments.title: Look up one key in sorted and unsorted files
experiments.question: Count and sum the events of a single user.

variants.name: files ordered by time
variants.sql: SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(amount) FROM events WHERE user_id = 1234567

variants.name: a copy sorted by user_id
variants.sql: SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(amount) FROM events_by_user WHERE user_id = 1234567
